newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba denies harassing U.S. diplomats.
newsitem.headline: Cuba denies harassing U.S. diplomats.

text.p: Cuba's Foreign Ministry denied on Thursday that Cuban authorities had harassed two U.S. diplomats after they met a dissident last week.

A U.S. government source said on Monday that Washington would protest to Cuba over an incident last Friday in which she said two U.S. diplomats were verbally harassed and had their vehicle tampered with after meeting dissident Olance Nogueras in the central town of Cienfuegos.

Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Marianela Ferriol told a weekly news briefing on Thursday there were no insults from Cuban authorities, no harassment, and at no point were the two diplomats in any danger.
She said false versions of what happened were apparently "fabricated in Miami," home to much of the Cuban-American community, and said the United States had added to these versions.
The U.S. source said the incident occurred when two officers from the United States Interests Section came out of a meeting with Nogueras, a dissident journalist.

She said the diplomats were filmed by a Cuban camera crew "undoubtedly from Cuban state security" and were verbally harassed, including being asked whether they felt threatened by damage to their vehicle.
One of their vehicle's tires was sabotaged and the camera crew filmed the diplomats repairing it, she added.

Cuban authorities have expressed irritation in the past at U.S. diplomats' active contacts with dissidents on the communist-ruled island. Havana last August expelled a U.S. diplomat, saying she had violated diplomatic conventions by supporting and organising anti-government opposition groups.
